newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - July gas oil down on prompt sell.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - July gas oil down on prompt sell.

text.p: Singapore front month gas oil swaps were down sharply at midday on Tuesday due to the aggressive prompt physical offers late Monday amid concerns of excess physical supplies, traders said.
"July gas oil is down because of the very low offers on Monday and the poor India award," a trader said.
July swaps gas oil were last quoted at $21.10/$21.25 per barrel compared to Monday's $21.50 offers, brokers said.
August was quoted at $21.90/$22.00, down from Monday's $22.00/$22.10, with deals done at $21.95, $22.00, they said.
As a result of relatively steady August values the July/August time spread widened as was quoted at minus 90-70 cents, brokers said.

Traders said the steep contango is reflective of the weak promp physical market were sellers are hard pressed to find markets in the face of poor demand from the region's big buyers such as China and India.
India sent prices down on Monday when the awared a meagre 165,000 tonnes of diesel for August delivery compared to 855,000 tonnes it bought for July arrival.
The award was also well below market expectations of about 400,000 tonnes as late as Friday evening, they said.
On its part, China has yet to reveal any signs that will enter the market soon in a big way to buy diesel for August.
Traders said the Chinese authorities have stepped up anti-smuggling checks in the face high domestic diesel production as refiners complain of poor returns due to the cheaper smuggled products.

Lower July swap prices was also triggered by the aggressive prompt physical offers late Monday where three cargoes were offered at around $21.30 per barrel free-on-board basis, down 45 cents from Friday's lowest offer.
The swaps jet/gas oil regrade was steady with July bid at $1.80, while the August/September regrade moved in to backwardation due to the steep contango in the gas oil market for the same two months.
August was quoted at $1.70/$1.90 and September at $1.60/$1.80, brokers said.
Fuel oil edged up slightly after Monday's strong physical support where a local trader bought two 20,000 tonne cargoes at $99.00 per tonne.
August and September swaps were quoted up 25 cents from Monday at $99.00/$99.50 per tonne, brokers said.
